title: MoPE: A Mixture of Password Experts for Improving Password Guessing
abstract: Textual passwords remain a predominant authentication mechanism in web security. To evaluate their strength, existing research has proposed several data-driven models across offline and online guessing scenarios. However, most of them treat passwords uniformly, neglecting the heterogeneous structural differences. This typically results in biased training that favors frequent password structural patterns. To mitigate this, we argue that passwords, as a type of complex short textual data, should be processed in a structure-aware manner by identifying their structural patterns and routing them to structure-specialized models accordingly. Motivated by this, we propose MOPE, a Mixture-of-Password-Experts framework, specifically designed to leverage the structural patterns in passwords for improving password modeling. Our MoPE introduces: (1) a novel structure-based method for generating specialized expert models; (2) a lightweight gating method for selecting appropriate expert models and outputting reliable guesses. Under the evaluated capped-training (100k samples) cross-dataset offline setting and the studied online passwordreuse setting, MOPE significantly outperforms strong baselines, achieving up to 38.80% and 9.34% improvement in cracking rate, respectively. This suggests that MOPE can effectively exploit heterogeneous structural patterns for password modeling in limited-training and distribution-shifted regimes. Furthermore, we implement a real-time Password Strength Meter (PSM) based on offline MOPE, assisting users in choosing stronger passwords more precisely with millisecond-level per-password response latency. Finally, using the online MoPE framework in the studied password-reuse setting, we uncover a risk pattern that passwords created under the examined complex password-composition policy are 60.1% more likely to be guessed.
